text: The game begins. Six players sit down at the table: Sonnet, Haiku, Gemma, Sol, Luna, Terra. Nobody knows who the killers are.
Night 1

Night falls on Palermo and everyone closes their eyes. The killers meet in the dark, and the officer is shown one of them. A new day dawns in Palermo. Nobody is out.

Night falls on Palermo. The killers strike, but the doctor got there first. A new day dawns in Palermo, and nobody is out.

text: Palermo has voted: Sonnet is out. Sonnet shows the card: killer.
The game is over. The town wins. The roles were: Sonnet the killer, Haiku the killer, Gemma the officer, Sol the doctor, Luna the citizen, Terra the citizen.

Gemma claimed to be the officer on day one and called Haiku a killer, and the town voted Haiku out, where he was revealed as a killer. On day two, Gemma reported checking Luna and finding her clean, and Sonnet and Terra traded accusations while Sol weighed both of them. The turning point came when Sonnet softened his suspicion of Terra once he was challenged, and Terra kept him talking until he slipped. Palermo then voted Sonnet out, revealing him as the second killer, and the town won with Sonnet and Haiku both exposed.
